newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Monday, on last Friday's gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at 20,280 yuan ($2,441) per tonne, rising 180 yuan. It opened at 20,200 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,170 and a high of 20,290.
September rose 100 to 21,020 yuan, October 90 to 20,600, November 190 to 20,370, the January 1997 contract 160 to 20,260, February 150 to 20,300 and March 150 to 20,350.
Combined volume fell to 16,490 tonnes from 20,655.
Copper opened up and rose for most of the session.
Traders said LME gains encouraged some long position holders but the overall outlook for copper was still negative.
"Gains on the LME was responsible for today's rises, but decreased volume indicated this was only a technical rebound," one trader said.
"Copper fell below the range of 20,500/21,000 last week, which indicated it would meet selling pressure in the short term," he added.
Traders said speculative buying was the main factor supporting copper in the short term due to a lack of news.
"A shortage of market-moving news has made copper consolidate in a narrow range, and sooner or later it will fall below 20,000-yuan level due to poor fundamantals," one trader said.
Most analysts said they expected copper to test the 20,000-yuan support level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down in slow trading. September fell 150 to 14,400 yuan, October 50 to 14,250, November 50 to 14,190.
Combined volume fell to 350 tonnes from 465.
